race_context: The 'Sheridan School Board' seats belong to Sheridan Community Schools, based in Sheridan in northwestern Hamilton County; the district's boundaries cover parts of both Hamilton and Boone counties {wfyi_2026}{nces_sheridan}. Federal data list 1,169 students in three schools in 2024-25 {nces_sheridan}. Dr. Dave Mundy is superintendent {reporter_ref_2026}.

The Board of Trustees has five members {reporter_2023}. Seats carry area labels: two Adams Township seats and an at-large seat were on the 2022 ballot, and two Marion Township (Boone County) seats were on the 2024 ballot, held then by Dan Fleming and John Hunt {hc_2022}{wfyi_2024}. Tyler Henning is board president {reporter_ref_2026}. This guide did not find the district's written election plan or a current board roster on the district website, which did not load during research.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: WFYI reports two Adams Township seats and one At Large seat, all three held by incumbents who are running again {wfyi_2026}. The state list shows the Adams Township race as 'vote for 1' {in_list}, but in 2022 the Hamilton County ballot listed it as 'vote for 2' {hc_2022}. If two Adams Township seats are elected, as WFYI reports, both Adams Township candidates would be seated.

2022 results (Hamilton County portion only): in Adams Township (vote for 2), Kim Zachery received 1,048 votes and Tyler Henning 826, and both were seated as new members {hc_2022}{reporter_2023}. In the At Large race, Nancy Boone received 686 votes, Cheri Hume 466 and Drew J Carlisle 290 {hc_2022}. The Reporter described Boone as representing Marion Township in Boone County and said 2022 was her second-term win {reporter_2023}. Boone County's share of the vote was not checked.

Party labels: 2026 is the first Hamilton County school board election under a state law that lets candidates list a party, list as independent or list no affiliation on the ballot {wfyi_2026}. Henning is listed as Independent; Zachery and Boone are listed as Nonpartisan on the state list and as 'no party' by WFYI {in_list}{wfyi_2026}.

Operating referendum on the same ballot (Nov. 3, 2026): Sheridan Community School Corporation asks voters to approve a property tax rate of up to $0.40 per $100 of assessed value for up to eight years, with a maximum annual levy of $2.9 million, to fund 'educational and operational stability in response to reductions in property tax revenue,' including teacher and staff retention, academic programs and operating costs {dlgf_sheridan}. The ballot question says a median residence of $250,000 would pay $454 more per year if it passes, and notes that the district's 2023 operating referendum passed {dlgf_sheridan}. The state approved the ballot language June 10, 2026 {dlgf_sheridan}.

Budget and SEA 1 (2025 property-tax law): in a district announcement, board president Henning said the new referendum 'was not part of our original long-range financial planning' and was needed because of Senate Enrolled Act 1; the district said the new rate would replace, not add to, the 2023 referendum rate and aims to keep the same level of referendum funding voters approved in 2023 {reporter_ref_2026}. The district said the 2023 referendum passed with about 84 percent support and that cost-saving measures had already cut several hundred thousand dollars this budget cycle {reporter_ref_2026}. That announcement gives the current and proposed rates per $1,000 of assessed value, while the state's ballot-language ruling states the proposed maximum as $0.40 per $100 {reporter_ref_2026}{dlgf_sheridan}.
Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or news coverage of the candidates' views.
